title: Laurent determinant column budgets
statement: Column exponent bounds add under determinants; one degree-one boundary column gives an upper degree-one bound. Faithful substitution can transfer that bound to a polynomial.
assumptions: Finite square matrix; appropriate commutative coefficient ring. Domain and nonvanishing leading-chart hypotheses for faithful substitution.
failure_mode: Two degree-one columns may yield degree two; unproved chart hypotheses cannot be omitted.
evidence_status: Lean source present; verification reported in PR #6

title: Two-layer subgraph capacity obstruction
statement: A selected subgraph exceeding the sum of two admissible layer capacities cannot be covered by those layers.
assumptions: Exact graph incidences and the displayed layer capacity assumptions; transfer from planar graphs requires the relevant graph theorem.
failure_mode: Passing the full-graph Euler bound does not imply biplanarity. Conditional capacities alone do not certify arbitrary planarity claims.

title: Two-frequency silent-subspace test
statement: In the finite lossless model, the divided response difference in a pole-free interval has the metric kernel. Two exact scalar zeros for one real direction imply zero coupling.
assumptions: Fixed positive gaps and positive residues, fixed transition numerators, real direction, distinct squared photon energies, no crossed pole.
failure_mode: Crossed poles, signed residues or changed response model can invalidate the implication; finite error bounds give a bound, not exact darkness.

title: Probe reconstruction or an invisible perturbation
statement: A target linear observable on real symmetric matrices is uniformly determined by probe readings iff its matrix lies in the span of their probe outer products.
assumptions: Fixed real symmetric matrix class and linear quadratic-form readings; special PSD boundary data require separate treatment.
failure_mode: A finite candidate-list identification does not prove identifiability over the full matrix class. Complex response requires imaginary cross probes.
